---
title: "Customize capture"
description: "Build your capture screens with your own components, copy, and camera controls."
---

Start with the [quickstart](/external/web), then replace its HTML and styles with your application’s components. The SDK attaches the camera to your video element and reports state changes through `onState`.

## Choose documents before opening the camera

Use `state.countryCodes` for the country selector. When the customer confirms a country, request its document choices:

```javascript
capture.start(state.scanId, undefined, selectedCountry);
```

Build your document selector from `state.allowedDocumentTypes`, filtered by `supportedDocumentTypes`. When the customer chooses a document and presses your camera button:

```javascript
capture.start(state.scanId, selectedDocumentType, selectedCountry);
```

Use ISO two-letter country codes, such as `US` or `GB`. Display the country’s localized name in your interface. See [Supported documents](/external/documents) for document labels and capture instructions.

## Style the camera view

The video element belongs to your page. Use CSS to size it and add a fixed guide above it:

```html
<div class="viewfinder">
  <video id="camera" autoplay playsinline muted></video>
  <div class="guide" aria-hidden="true"></div>
</div>
```

```css
.viewfinder { position: relative; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 16px; }
.viewfinder video { display: block; width: 100%; }
.guide { position: absolute; inset: 8%; border: 2px solid white; border-radius: 12px; pointer-events: none; }
.guide.ready { border-color: #16a34a; }
```

Set the guide’s ready state from `Guidance.HOLD_STILL`. Place the current instruction in a `role="status"` element above the viewfinder. Use a card-shaped guide for IDs and a page-shaped guide for passports.

## Show the next required side

Read `requiredSides` and `acceptedSides` to find the next image to request:

```javascript
const nextSide = state.requiredSides.find(side => !state.acceptedSides.includes(side));
```

For an ID, label the side **Back of ID** or **Front of ID**. For a passport, ask for its photo page. Update the instruction when the state changes; the capture sequence depends on the document and your venue settings.

## Add a capture button

Automatic capture is enabled by default. An optional button lets the customer request a capture manually:

```javascript
captureButton.onclick = () => capture.capture();
```

Show the button during `Phase.CAPTURING`. The SDK checks the current frame before accepting a manual capture.

## Add a flashlight button

Pass `onTorchChange` when creating the SDK instance. Show the button when `available` is true and use `enabled` to render its current state:

```javascript
onTorchChange({ available, enabled }) {
  flashlightButton.hidden = !available;
  flashlightButton.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(enabled));
  flashlightButton.onclick = async () => {
    try {
      await capture.setTorch(!enabled);
    } catch {
      flashlightMessage.textContent = 'Flashlight unavailable. Try a brighter area.';
    }
  };
}
```

## Localize instructions

Map `Guidance` and `ErrorCode` values to your message catalog. Use the SDK values to choose an action and your translated copy to explain it. The [troubleshooting guide](/external/recovery) provides suggested messages and recovery actions.

## Clean up on navigation

Call `capture.destroy()` when your component unmounts or the capture page closes. Call `capture.stop()` for a cancel button when you want to keep the instance available.
